title: Separation of Paloma Business Accounts and Personal Accounts
content:
The accounts of one owner are never pooled. A Paloma Business account stands on its own, and it stands apart from the owner's Personal Sender Account.

### Rules of separation

1. Each Paloma Business account's balance funds only that account's payouts and fees.
2. Volume limits, allowances and seats are counted per Paloma Business account.
3. Money moves between two of the owner's Paloma Business accounts only as a withdrawal to a bank account and a fresh deposit.
4. A payout or withdrawal is taken only from the balance of the account it is submitted on. The account it is submitted on is identified by its Paloma Business account reference in the system records, and the test is made before the payout or withdrawal is taken.
5. Withdrawals go only to the business's own verified US bank account, never to the owner personally.
6. A Paloma Business account and the owner's Personal Sender Account are separate contracts: business payouts never count toward personal sending limits, personal transfers never use the business balance or allowance, and Paloma Rewards points are never earned on business payouts.

### Basis Q&A

**Can a payout submitted on one Paloma Business account be paid from the balance of the owner's other Paloma Business account?** No. A payout is taken only from the balance of the account it is submitted on.

**How does an owner move money from one of their Paloma Business accounts to another?** Only as a withdrawal to a bank account followed by a fresh deposit into the other account.

**Do free payouts or the monthly volume limit of two accounts of the same owner add together?** No. Allowances and volume limits are counted per account.

**Does a business payout use up the owner's personal sending limit?** No. Business payouts never count toward personal sending limits.

**Can a personal transfer be paid from the Paloma Business balance?** No. Personal transfers never use the business balance or allowance.

**Are Paloma Rewards points earned on business payouts?** No, never.
